newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Still no C&W approach on Optus-Australia govt.
newsitem.headline: Still no C&W approach on Optus-Australia govt.

text.p: British telecommunications firm Cable and Wireless Plc still had not approached the Australian government about lifting its stake in Optus Communications Pty Ltd, a government spokesman said on Monday.
"To my knowledge, we haven't received a formal approach from them," a spokesman for Communications Minister Richard Alston told Reuters.
Newspaper reports last week said Cable and Wireless (C&W) wanted to double its stake in Optus to 49 percent through the buy-out of BellSouth Corp Inc's 24.5 percent holding in the company.
On Monday, The Australian newspaper said an announcement about Cable and Wireless' A$1 billion-plus deal to buy BellSouth's Optus holding could come as soon as today.
C&W needs approval for such a move from Australia's Foreign Investment Review Board, which answers to Treasurer Peter Costello.
Alston's spokesman said the minister was planning to meet with C&W executives in the United Kingdom later this month to discuss on-line services and telecoms deregulation.
"If there was something that they wished to discuss with him, maybe they could do it then," the spokesman said.
The major Optus shareholder is Australian transport and healthcare group Mayne Nickless Ltd, which had hoped to sell its stake later this year in conjunction with a float.

Earlier this month, Optus appointed former C&W executive Peter Howell-Davies as its chief executive officer, replacing Ziggy Switkowski, who resigned after a year of rising losses at Optus' pay television operations.
These losses and the management change has forced the indefinite postponement of the float.
